A chapter-opening photograph showing a health worker seated at a table sorting through yellow paper health record booklets, with a mobile phone also on the table. Behind her, a wall mural illustrates degrees of child malnutrition (three numbered figures with Kinyarwanda captions) and a mother breastfeeding an infant.

A chapter-opening photograph, shown rotated 180 degrees, of two hands holding a smartphone displaying a Vietnamese-language mobile web page with a login field, held over an open paper ledger of handwritten patient records.

Figure 2.3, a screenshot of the K4Health "Toolkits" website's Frameworks page within the Measuring Success Toolkit, showing the site's navigation bar and a page listing framework types: Conceptual Frameworks, Results Frameworks, Logical Frameworks and Logic Models, alongside a right-hand sidebar menu.

Figure 2.5, a diagram of the MOTECH Mobile Midwife and Client Data Application. A central icon of a mobile network tower sits inside a circle, with arrows connecting it to three panels: a top panel showing icons of a mother and child and a health worker, each with a mobile phone, linked by an arrow representing reminder messages; a left panel showing mother icons with phones; and a right panel showing a health-worker icon with a phone alongside icons of a book and a house, representing the exchange of client and care data between mobile users and the central platform.

A screenshot of a journal article page titled "Conceptual models for health education research and practice" by Jo Anne Earp and Susan T. Ennett, showing the article's byline, affiliations and abstract text, illustrating the source cited in the text for conceptual frameworks.

The cover of a USAID Performance Monitoring & Evaluation "TIPS" publication titled "Building a Results Framework," showing the series title, an issue number, and a contents summary including sections "What is a results framework?" and "Why is the results framework important?"
The cover of the "Maternal and Newborn Standards and Indicators Compendium," showing the title, USAID and CORE logos, and a grid of four photographs of mothers and infants.

A screenshot of a DHS Program website page, showing its blue header navigation bar and a page of publication text, illustrating the source cited for DHS survey indicators on maternal and child health.

The cover of the "Indicator and Monitoring Framework for the Global Strategy for Women's, Children's and Adolescents' Health (2016-2030)" publication by Every Woman Every Child, showing the title in white text on a dark background with the initiative's logo.
A screenshot of a DHS Program website page, showing its header navigation bar and body text, illustrating the source cited for the HIV/AIDS Survey Indicators Database.

A title slide reading "1. Health service delivery" over a photograph of two health workers at an outdoor market-style facility, with a row of numbered icons across the top indicating this is one slide in a numbered series.

A screenshot of a MEASURE Evaluation web page titled "Service Delivery - Quality of Care / Service Provision Assessment," showing the site's blue header and a short summary of the resource with a download link.
A screenshot of a MEASURE Evaluation web page titled "Summary List of Indicators," showing the site's blue header, a left-hand navigation menu, and a list of linked indicator categories.

The cover of a publication titled "National AIDS Programmes: A guide to indicators for monitoring and evaluating national HIV/AIDS prevention programmes for young people," showing the title text on a red ribbon-patterned background with logos of UNAIDS, UNICEF, WHO and other partner organizations along the bottom.

The cover of a publication titled "National AIDS Programmes: A guide to monitoring and evaluation," issued by UNAIDS, showing the title text and a UNAIDS document reference number on a plain background.

A chapter-opening photograph, taken from above, of a health worker's hands and torso at a desk covered with a blue floral cloth. The hands rest on a smartphone placed inside an open handwritten notebook, next to a printed tabular data sheet, pens, a ruler and other stationery.
A very thin (3 pixels wide) vertical strip of mixed colour; the extracted fragment is too narrow to convey any content, and what it depicts could not be determined from the extracted image.

Figure 3.4, a screenshot of the cStock monitoring dashboard, showing a top navigation bar with tabs including Dashboard, Stock Status, Alert Summary and Order Fill Rate; a left-hand "Stockout rates" panel listing districts with percentages of health facilities reporting at least one stockout; a "Current alerts" panel with percentages for categories such as orders that cannot be resupplied and pending orders; a "Reporting rates" chart combining stacked bars (coloured by on-time, late, not reported and complete status) with an overlaid line showing percentage reported over time; and a right-hand "Current National Picture" panel for Malawi giving counts of districts, facilities and registered users alongside a per-product stock-out rate table.

Figure 3.6, a scanned quality-control checklist titled "TextIT Mentor Mother Competency Checklist," with fields for trainee name, designation and date, a Y/N rating key (Understood / Needs more training), and a table of skills grouped under six sections (basic understanding of HIV/AIDS, PMTCT and safe motherhood and infant care; understanding of the TextIT study; study SOPs; study logs; data collection using smartphone; and other responsibilities at work), each skill row having Rating and Comments columns. The smartphone-related skills under Section 5, such as switching the phone on and off, identifying the ODK application, and entering, editing, saving and sending data using ODK, are highlighted in a red-outlined callout box, alongside Section 6's item on facilitating HIV education.

A chapter-opening photograph of a desktop computer monitor on an office desk, displaying a Vietnamese-language web application for immunization registration and reporting, with a child's record open showing personal details and a vaccination schedule table. Stacks of paper forms, a mouse and a telephone are visible on the desk around the monitor.
The cover of the "WHO Evaluation Practice Handbook," published by the World Health Organization, showing the title in white text over a marbled blue-grey background with the WHO emblem.

The cover of "Impact Evaluation in Practice" by Paul J. Gertler, Sebastian Martinez, Patrick Premand, Laura B. Rawlings and Christel M. J. Vermeersch, published by the World Bank, showing the title over a pattern of connected dots on a dark background.
A chapter-opening photograph of a health worker in a white headscarf and coat entering data on a mobile phone, with a young child in traditional dress in soft focus in the foreground.
A very thin (3 pixels wide) vertical strip of mixed colour; the extracted fragment is too narrow to convey any content, and what it depicts could not be determined from the extracted image.

A screenshot of a MEASURE Evaluation web page titled "Inventory of PRISM Framework and Tools: Application of PRISM Tools and Interventions for Strengthening Routine Health Information System Performance," showing the site's header, main navigation and a right-hand sidebar with search-publications and shopping-cart controls.

A chapter-opening photograph of a clinic room in which a seated woman patient faces two health workers across a desk cluttered with medical supplies and paperwork; one worker, seated, points to a tablet computer screen, while the other stands behind, and a poster and wooden cabinet are visible on the wall behind them.

Figure 6.1, four screenshots of the Mobilize mobile phone application's "Followup Visit" screens, labelled A through D. Panel A ("Patient data") lists checkbox symptoms including vision loss, deafness and ringing in ears; panel B ("Vision group") asks yes/no questions about eye pain, light sensitivity and decreased vision; panel C asks how long a symptom has been occurring, with choices from "past day" to ">1 month"; and panel D ("What is your overall assessment?") offers options of needs urgent care, follow-up at next appointment or prescription required, or stable with no medical attention needed.
A printed barcode with the ISBN number 9789241511766 beneath it.
